claims.text: On the path graph with N >= 2 vertices n_1, ..., n_N and edges n_i n_{i+1}, (A^k)_{1N} = 0 for k < N-1 and (A^{N-1})_{1N} = 1; hence a sum A + ... + A^m with m < N-1 has a zero at (1,N) although the graph is connected. Proof: each step of a walk changes the vertex index by 1, so a walk from n_1 to n_N needs at least N-1 steps, and the only walk of length N-1 is n_1, ..., n_N; the walk-counting theorem converts this to matrix entries. Supersedes the experimental illustration M3-7 as the justification that the limit N-1 cannot be lowered.

claims.text: On the five-town map (edges n1n2, n1n3, n1n5, n2n3, n2n4, n3n4, n3n5, n4n5) the degrees are 3,3,4,3,3. A trail of length 8 uses all 8 edges once; each vertex other than the ends is entered and left equally often, so it has even degree; the map has four odd-degree vertices, so no trail of length 8 exists. This explains the 0 in the k = 8 trail count of the table of walks, trails and paths.
